title: Docker Networking
subtitle: Drivers, DNS, isolation and connectivity debugging
description: Networks are where most "it works on my machine" bugs live. Learn the drivers, how Docker DNS resolves service names, and how to debug a connection systematically.
outcomes: Create user-defined bridge networks with DNS
Debug connectivity with inspect, exec and logs

lessons.title: Network drivers
lessons.summary: bridge, host, overlay, macvlan, ipvlan and none: what each is for.
objectives: Match a driver to a use case
Know the security implications of host networking

sections.title: Bridge is the default
sections.body:
A bridge network is a virtual switch on the host. Containers get veth pairs and an IP on the bridge. The default `bridge` network exists automatically, but user-defined bridge networks are preferred because they provide automatic DNS resolution by container name.

`host` removes network isolation: the container shares the host stack, so port mappings are ignored and conflicts are immediate. `overlay` spans multiple hosts (Swarm). `macvlan` gives containers real MAC addresses on the physical network. `none` disables networking entirely.

sections.caption: The host bridge connects containers to each other and, through NAT, to external networks.

sections.title: Host networking bypasses isolation
sections.body: A host-network container can bind any host port and reach localhost services. Avoid it unless you need the host stack and understand the blast radius.

exercises.title: Create a user network
exercises.prompt: Create a bridge network named app-net and inspect its subnet.
exercises.expected: docker network create app-net; docker network inspect app-net.

exercises.title: Isolate
exercises.prompt: Run a container with no network and prove it cannot resolve DNS.
exercises.command: docker run --rm --network none alpine sh -c "getent hosts example.com || echo isolated"
exercises.expected: docker run --rm --network none alpine ping -c1 1.1.1.1 fails.

questions.explain: Host networking removes the network namespace boundary.

questions.explain: Overlay spans hosts in a Swarm.

lessons.title: Bridge networks and DNS
lessons.summary: How service names resolve, why the default bridge behaves differently, and how aliases work.
objectives: Connect containers to a user-defined network
Resolve services by name and alias

sections.title: Embedded DNS
sections.body:
On a user-defined network, Docker runs an embedded DNS server at `127.0.0.11` inside each container. It resolves container names and network aliases to current container IPs. This is what makes `postgres:5432` work in Compose without hard-coded IPs.

On the default bridge, only IP addresses and `--link` (legacy) work. Always create a user-defined network for multi-container applications.

sections.code:
docker network create app-net
docker run -d --name db --network app-net postgres:16-alpine \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret
docker run -d --name api --network app-net my-api:1.0

# from inside api, the name db resolves
docker exec api getent hosts db
docker exec api node -e "require('net').connect(5432,'db').on('connect',()=>{console.log('ok');process.exit(0)})"

# attach an existing container to a second network
docker network connect app-net api
docker network inspect app-net

sections.title: Aliases let you rename services
sections.body: `--network-alias database` adds another DNS name. Compose uses this for service aliases and stable naming.

exercises.title: Name resolution
exercises.prompt: Create two containers on a user-defined network and resolve one from the other.
exercises.expected: getent hosts SERVICE returns the other container IP.

exercises.title: Alias
exercises.prompt: Add alias database to a container named db on app-net.
exercises.command: docker network connect --alias database app-net db
exercises.expected: docker network connect --alias database app-net db

lessons.title: Lab: connect two services
lessons.summary: Build a two-container application network from scratch and prove connectivity both ways.
objectives: Create a network and attach containers
Inspect and clean up network resources

sections.title: The scenario
sections.body: Run Redis and a client container on a private network. Confirm the client resolves `cache` and can reach port 6379. Then connect the client to a second network and observe the additional interface.

items.title: Start Redis
items.body: Run redis:7-alpine with the name `cache` on that network.

items.title: Test DNS and TCP
items.body: From an alpine client, resolve `cache` and use `nc -z cache 6379`.

items.title: Inspect
items.body: Inspect the network and find both container IPs.

items.title: Clean up
items.body: Remove the containers and the network.

sections.code:
docker network create opsdeck-net
docker run -d --name cache --network opsdeck-net redis:7-alpine
docker run --rm --network opsdeck-net alpine sh -c 'getent hosts cache && nc -z cache 6379 && echo reachable'
docker network inspect opsdeck-net --format '{{range .Containers}}{{.Name}} {{.IPv4Address}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
docker rm -f cache
docker network rm opsdeck-net

sections.title: Network cleanup is automatic… eventually
sections.body: Removing the last container can leave a user-defined network behind. Remove it explicitly when you are done, or let Compose manage it.

exercises.title: Second network
exercises.prompt: Connect the running cache container to a second network.
exercises.command: docker network create other-net && docker network connect other-net cache

exercises.title: Clean up
exercises.prompt: Remove the containers and both networks.
exercises.expected: docker rm -f cache; docker network rm opsdeck-net other-net

questions.question: Why does cache resolve without --link?
options: Both containers are on a user-defined network
questions.explain: User-defined networks use Docker embedded DNS.

questions.question: What command tests TCP reachability?
questions.explain: nc -z attempts a TCP connection without sending data.

questions.question: Where can you find container IPs on a network?
questions.explain: Network inspect lists connected containers and addresses.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting connectivity
lessons.summary: A repeatable checklist for "the container cannot reach the database".
objectives: Debug DNS, routing and port binding separately

sections.title: Separate the layers
sections.body: Debug in order: (1) are the containers on the same network? (2) does the name resolve? (3) is the target process listening on the expected interface? (4) is the port published? (5) is a host firewall or proxy interfering? Most incidents are a mismatch in one of these layers, not a Docker bug.

sections.code:
# 1. Network membership
docker inspect api --format '{{json .NetworkSettings.Networks}}'
docker network inspect app-net --format '{{range .Containers}}{{.Name}} {{.IPv4Address}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'

# 2. DNS from inside the client
docker exec api getent hosts db

# 3. Is the listener bound correctly?
docker exec db sh -c 'netstat -lntp 2>/dev/null || ss -lntp'
# A process bound to 127.0.0.1 inside the container is NOT reachable by other containers.

# 4. Published port
docker port api
curl -v http://127.0.0.1:8080/health

# 5. Ephemeral debug container on the same network
docker run --rm --network app-net nicolaka/netshoot \
  sh -c 'dig db +short; nc -zv db 5432'
sections.note: netshoot is a popular debug image; in restricted environments use alpine with busybox tools instead.

sections.title: Do not "fix" networking with host mode
sections.body: Switching to host networking hides the real problem and destroys isolation. Fix DNS, bind addresses, or network membership instead.

exercises.title: Layer checklist
exercises.prompt: A web container cannot reach db:5432. List the first four checks in order.
exercises.expected: Same network → DNS resolves → listener on 0.0.0.0 → published/port correct.

exercises.title: Find the bind address
exercises.prompt: Inspect a Postgres container and explain why it might listen only on localhost.
exercises.expected: The postgres config listen_addresses may be localhost; set it to * or the container interface.

questions.question: A service listens on 127.0.0.1:5432 inside its container. Can another container reach it?
options: No, it is bound to loopback
questions.explain: Loopback inside the container is not reachable from other namespaces.

questions.question: Which command shows which networks a container is attached to?
What is the first thing to check for name resolution failures?
options: Whether both containers share a user-defined network
questions.explain: Embedded DNS only works on user-defined networks.
